The evaluator never reads check.files: its verdict is computed only over the bindings the author chose (apps/operator/scripts/__tests__/phone-app-{edge,hosted}-config*.test.ts, the operational doc docs/evidence/phone-p002-browser-voice-2026-10-06.json, and one mutation probe). testing:runs shows a latest PASS for all 10 registered files, but three last ran on 2026-10-02 (20521450, 20541403, 20487246), so their current-source status is unproven. This case therefore does not flip; a red or stale registered file would still grade pass.\n\nSecondary signal, same proof-accounting gap: the card's '8 immutable binding(s)' includes test-run-group:28cb7a49...:1/:3/:5 (bindings 26766/26768/26770). Those resolve to the same testRunIds 20844203/20844202/20844204 already bound by file ref, so there are only 5 distinct runs. The e2e layer is met by an operational evidence doc whose own specs field lists AUTO-BAR-R-2-P-002@3 / R-13 / PHONE-P-002-OUTCOME, not R-74, while the r-74 intent says live/manual verification and the automated suite must not substitute for each other.\n\nProposed fix: when a clause's sourceBar has check.kind='tests', have correct-layer / plan-class-risk-floor (or a new census) require a current passing binding for each check.files entry, or rate unknown with the missing list. Dedupe bindings by testRunId before counting. Seen during the grading-integrity audit of EI-25211993321802878 by judge session su-bc328b06 on 2026-10-06.\n\nWhat I saw: from 06:54:10Z to 06:59:30Z (about 5.5 min), almost every papercusp MCP response carried `_dataPlaneMayBeDegraded: \"⚠ DATA PLANE MAY BE DEGRADED: this session's local MCP proxy observed an upstream retry or connection failure at <ts>\"`. The timestamp moved forward each time (06:54:10.741, 06:54:12.338, 06:54:41.152, 06:54:48.309, 06:55:01.543, 06:56:06.161, 06:59:10.001, 06:59:30.374). But every call it was attached to came back ok:true with complete data. That includes scorecards:get, plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy, testing:runs, scorecards:emit (created EI-25212339002058655) and improvements:capture.\n\nThere are two possibilities, and I could not tell which is true:\n(a) The proxy really does retry or reconnect upstream (for example, a :3070/:3170 restart, or a stale connection in the pool) on about every call. That is a hidden latency and reliability problem.\n(b) The warning window keeps getting re-armed by something other than this session's own calls failing. That is a false alarm, and it trains agents to ignore the warning.\n\nHow to tell them apart: log, per proxy request, whether this request itself hit a retry. Then compare that with the warning stamp. The response contained `{\"ok\":true,\"state\":{\"full\":{...truncated...}},\"_partial\":true,\"_projection\":{...}}`.
